fact: Blumberger et al., Lancet 2018;391:1683-92. Randomised, multicentre, non-inferiority; 414 allocated (205 10 Hz rTMS, 209 iTBS); primary HRSD-17 change. HRSD-17 23.5->13.4 (10 Hz) vs 23.6->13.4 (iTBS); adjusted difference 0.103 (lower 95% CI -1.16), iTBS non-inferior (margin 2.25). Session ~3 min vs 37.5 min.
note: Read via Europe PMC record of PMID 29726344 (PubMed and PMC blocked by captcha). Commentary at https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6026669/ agreed.

fact: Final order, 83 FR 66103 (Dec 26, 2018), Docket FDA-2014-N-1210, 21 CFR 882 (product code GXC), effective Dec 26, 2018. Class II with special controls: ECT for catatonia, or severe MDE associated with MDD or bipolar disorder, in patients age 13+ who are treatment-resistant OR require rapid response due to severity of psychiatric/medical condition. Remain Class III (PMA): schizophrenia, schizoaffective, schizophreniform, bipolar manic states; catatonia/severe MDE under age 13; and age 13+ not treatment-resistant and not needing rapid response. fact: Anand et al., NEJM 2023;388:2315-25 (online May 24, 2023). Open-label RCT, noninferiority, 403 randomized at 5 sites (200 ketamine, 203 ECT; 195 and 170 treated). Treatment-resistant MDD without psychosis. ECT 3x/week vs IV ketamine 0.5 mg/kg over 40 min 2x/week for 3 weeks. Primary: QIDS-SR16 response (>=50%). Response 55.4% ketamine vs 41.2% ECT, difference 14.2 pts (95% CI 3.9-24.2), noninferior (margin -10, P<0.001). ECT: decline in delayed verbal recall (HVLT-R mean change -9.7 vs -0.9) with gradual recovery; QoL similar; ECT musculoskeletal AEs, ketamine dissociation. NCT03113968.
note: Europe PMC record of PMID 37224232; NEJM site itself did not load. Ketamine at 0.5 mg/kg; ECT was right unilateral ultrabrief initial (not read from page - verify).

fact: CMS NCD 160.18: coverage of FDA-approved VNS for TRD only under Coverage with Evidence Development, in a CMS-approved double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial with >=1 year follow-up (may extend to prospective longitudinal study); non-covered outside CED. Services on/after Feb 15, 2019. Study criteria: MDE >=2 yr or >=4 episodes, 4 failed adequate treatments, stable meds 4 weeks, exclusions (psychosis, rapid-cycling bipolar, etc.); placebo group offered active VNS at end; replacement device covered for battery end-of-life/malfunction. Page shows 'older version' banner.

fact: Blinded 12-month unipolar cohort missed primary endpoint (MADRS response active vs sham, p<0.023 threshold) due to strong sham response; some secondaries significant. Announced June 6, 2024. Jan 13, 2026 Int J Neuropsychopharmacol (doi 10.1093/ijnp/pyaf080) 24-month open-label analysis of 214 actively-treated: ~69% response (>=30%) at 12 mo on at least one measure; 39 (>20%) in remission at 24 mo. Bipolar cohort ongoing as of 2024.
note: 2024 result read on LivaNova press release (company). 2026 paper described in https://www.news-medical.net/news/20260113/Implanted-vagus-nerve-stimulation-device-offers-lasting-relief-for-severe-depression.aspx (secondary; journal not opened). Whether CMS has reconsidered the NCD after 2024 not verified.

fact: Final order 84 FR 70003 (Dec 20, 2019), Docket FDA-2014-N-1209, 21 CFR 882: CES for anxiety and insomnia = Class II with special controls (510(k)); CES for depression = Class III, PMA required (due Mar 19, 2020). Existing anxiety/insomnia devices had until Dec 21, 2020 for 510(k) amendment.

CONFIRMED but as PMA approval, not clearance: Flow Neuroscience FL-100, PMA P230024, decision Dec 8, 2025, product code JXK (cranial electrotherapy stimulator group; FDA lists it as a CES-type device for depression). Indication: moderate to severe MDD in current episode, monotherapy or adjunctive, age 18+, not treatment-refractory to medication. SSED: Empower RCT week 10 (mITT 87 active/86 sham): primary HDRS-17 difference 2.3 pts (p=0.012); MADRS change -11.3 vs -7.7; response 63.0% vs 31.6%; remission 57.5% vs 29.4% (MADRS secondary, nominal p). Unblinding: 77.6% active guessed correctly vs 40.7% sham. One supplement S001.
note: SSED read at https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf23/P230024B.pdf. Home-use. Press (yahoo) said 'cleared'; correct term is approved (PMA).

fact: Medtronic Activa/Reclaim DBS Therapy for OCD, HDE H050003; FDA page decision date 02/10/2009 (SSPB text and press cite Feb 19, 2009). Indication: bilateral stimulation of the anterior limb of the internal capsule, adjunct to medication and alternative to anterior capsulotomy, adults with chronic severe treatment-resistant OCD who failed at least 3 SSRIs. Evidence: 26 patients at 4 centers; 12-mo YBOCS reduction ~41%; 10 full responders (>=35% reduction) and 4 partial among n=21 at 12 months; randomized blinded phase 62% vs 8%. Serious AEs 42.3%. HDE status = probable benefit, not proven effectiveness.
note: Date discrepancy in sources; verify against approval order. SSPB: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf5/H050003b.pdf. IRB oversight condition (standard for HDE) not stated in summary read; not verified. Target is ALIC/VC, correct usage 'anterior limb of internal capsule'.

fact: Holtzheimer et al., Lancet Psychiatry 2017;4(11):839-849. Multisite randomised sham-controlled SCC white-matter DBS for TRD (NCT00617162). 90 randomised (60 active, 30 sham) before futility analysis; response (>=40% reduction months 4-6) 20% (12/60) vs 17% (5/30), not significant. 6 months double-blind then open label. Trial stopped after futility analysis (stopping not confirmed on page read).
note: Abstract-level page on an aggregator; journal not opened. Early termination reported widely (e.g. neurocritic blog) but not confirmed on cited page.
